title: Test a reading against the next passage
statement: Have students commit to one of two plausible explanations, predict what the next passage will show, then read it and revise their account.
detail: An advanced-learning resource written for the Grade 9 unit proposes that students construct competing explanations, predict what each would imply, then confront new evidence that may undermine their preferred reading, with teaching that shows how to tell apart explanations that both sound convincing at first (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, line 2624). Its worked lesson starts with two plausible explanations of a character's changing trust, requires predictions about the next exchange, reveals the passage and makes students revise their account (line 2630). The resource was endorsed as the basis for the build (line 2705).
against: It is untested with students, and the resource says the new evidence "may" undermine the preferred reading, so a revision follows only where the reading fails (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, line 2624).
